canonicalization.canonical_form: UTF-8 bytes of json.dumps(parsed_corpus, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True), no trailing newline
canonicalization.corpus_canonical_sha256_is: SHA-256 of canonical_form; independent of file formatting
canonicalization.excluded: timestamps, UUIDs, absolute paths, user names, checker output
canonicalization.file_form: json.dumps(parsed_corpus, sort_keys=True, indent=2, ensure_ascii=True) + LF; corpus_file_sha256 is the SHA-256 of these exact LF bytes

contract_sha256_note: SHA-256 of the clarified contract file bytes (LF) in the working tree at lock time
derivation_order: Contract (clarified) -> Corpus v2 cases -> Expected verdicts -> Hash lock -> (later) Checker implementation
lock_statement: The expected verdicts in corpus_file are pre-registered and fixed by corpus_canonical_sha256. They may not be changed to match any checker result. A change requires a new corpus_id/version, a new record and a Human decision. The v1 corpus and record are retained unmodified.
verification_instructions: certutil -hashfile docs/architecture/phase-4/c1-negative-corpus-v2.json SHA256   must equal corpus_file_sha256 (LF bytes; a CRLF checkout changes this value, not corpus_canonical_sha256)
Recompute corpus_canonical_sha256 with any JSON tool following canonical_form
